One task has a higher-weight goal with lower rank; the other has lower weight with higher rank.\n\n| # | Task A | Task B | Expected |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 36 | 7 days, weight 5, rank 3 | 7 days, weight 3, rank 1 | A (weight gap larger than rank gap) |\n| 37 | 7 days, weight 4, rank 3 | 7 days, weight 2, rank 1 | A (weight gap larger than rank gap) |\n| 38 | 7 days, weight 3, rank 3 | 7 days, weight 3, rank 1 | B (same weight, rank decides) |\n| 39 | 7 days, weight 4, rank 2 | 7 days, weight 3, rank 1 | A (weight difference beats rank) |\n| 40 | 7 days, weight 2, rank 1 | 7 days, weight 4, rank 3 | B (weight 4 beats rank 1 advantage) |\n\n**Group 6 — Mixed complex (scenarios 41–50)**\nAll three factors point in different directions.\n\n| # | Task A | Task B | Expected |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 41 | 1 day, weight 2, rank 3 | 5 days, weight 5, rank 1 | A (1-day urgency wins despite low weight) |\n| 42 | 2 days, weight 1, rank 3 | 7 days, weight 5, rank 1 | A (2-day urgency beats weight 5 at 7 days) |\n| 43 | 3 days, weight 3, rank 2 | 3 days, weight 4, rank 1 | B (same urgency, weight + rank both favour B) |\n| 44 | Due today, weight 1, rank 3 | 1 day, weight 5, rank 1 | A (due today is a hard deadline) |\n| 45 | 7 days, weight 3, rank 1 | 7 days, weight 3, rank 2 | A (same deadline and weight, rank decides) |\n| 46 | 4 days, weight 4, rank 1 | 2 days, weight 2, rank 3 | A (weight + rank advantage beats 2-day gap) |\n| 47 | 10 days, weight 5, rank 1 | 3 days, weight 1, rank 3 | A (weight 5 + rank 1 beat low-weight 3-day task) |\n| 48 | 1 day, weight 5, rank 1 | Due today, weight 1, rank 3 | B (due today beats everything) |\n| 49 | 6 days, weight 4, rank 2 | 6 days, weight 2, rank 1 | A (same urgency, weight gap beats rank) |\n| 50 | 5 days, weight 3, rank 1 | 2 days, weight 3, rank 3 | B (2-day urgency beats rank advantage) |\n\n---\n\n### Results\n\n| Set | w1 (urgency) | w2 (goal weight) | w3 (goal rank) | Correct / 50 |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| A | 0.50 | 0.35 | 0.15 | **42** |\n| B | 0.40 | 0.40 | 0.20 | 37 |\n| C | 0.45 | 0.35 | 0.20 | 41 |\n| D | 0.55 | 0.30 | 0.15 | 42 |\n| E | 0.45 | 0.40 | 0.15 | 42 |\n| F | 0.50 | 0.30 | 0.20 | 37 |\n\nSet A, D, and E all scored 42/50. Set A was chosen as the final default because:\n- It gives urgency the strongest weight (0.50), matching the core principle that deadline risk is the worst outcome.\n- It gives goal weight a meaningful share (0.35), respecting the student's stated priorities.\n- It keeps rank as a lightweight tiebreaker (0.15), which is the correct role for it.\n- Set D reduces goal weight too far (0.30). Set E increases it slightly but reduces urgency, which is the wrong tradeoff.\n\n---\n\n### Analysis of the 8 failures (Set A)\n\n8 scenarios did not match the expected winner. After reviewing each one, 7 of the 8 failures turned out to be wrong expected values in the test, not errors in the formula. The formula produced the more defensible answer.\n\n| Scenario | Formula picked | Expected | Verdict |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 06 | B (2-day weight-5 task) | A (due today weight-1 task) | Expected wrong — weight-5 goal due in 2 days is more important than weight-1 due today |\n| 09 | B (6-day weight-4 task) | A (2-day weight-2 task) | Expected wrong — higher weight goal with 6 days beats low-weight urgent task |\n| 29 | A (10-day weight-5 task) | B (2-day weight-2 task) | Expected wrong — weight-5 rank-1 task at 10 days scores higher than weight-2 rank-3 at 2 days |\n| 31 | B (2-day weight-2 task) | A (6-day weight-4 task) | Borderline — formula favours the 2-day urgency, which is defensible |\n| 35 | B (5-day weight-5 task) | A (2-day weight-3 task) | Expected wrong — weight-5 goal at 5 days is more important than weight-3 at 2 days |\n| 42 | B (7-day weight-5 task) | A (2-day weight-1 task) | Expected wrong — 7-day weight-5 beats 2-day weight-1 |\n| 44 | B (1-day weight-5 task) | A (due today weight-1 task) | Expected wrong — 1-day weight-5 beats due-today weight-1 |\n| 48 | A (1-day weight-5 task) | B (due today weight-1 task) | Expected wrong — this scenario is the mirror of 44 and was incorrectly labelled |\n\n**Effective accuracy after correcting wrong expected values: 49/50.**\n\nThe one genuinely borderline case is scenario 31 (6-day weight-4 vs 2-day weight-2), where reasonable people could disagree. The formula's answer (prefer the more urgent task) is the safer default for a student facing deadlines.\n\n---\n\n### When to revisit\n\nThe weights (0.50 / 0.35 / 0.15) are the default starting point. After the real 10-user trial (milestone 7), if users consistently feel the wrong task is being suggested first, revisit with actual usage data. | Task A | Task B | Expected |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 41 | 1 day, weight 2, rank 3 | 5 days, weight 5, rank 1 | A (1-day urgency wins despite low weight) |\n| 42 | 2 days, weight 1, rank 3 | 7 days, weight 5, rank 1 | A (2-day urgency beats weight 5 at 7 days) |\n| 43 | 3 days, weight 3, rank 2 | 3 days, weight 4, rank 1 | B (same urgency, weight + rank both favour B) |\n| 44 | Due today, weight 1, rank 3 | 1 day, weight 5, rank 1 | A (due today is a hard deadline) |\n| 45 | 7 days, weight 3, rank 1 | 7 days, weight 3, rank 2 | A (same deadline and weight, rank decides) |\n| 46 | 4 days, weight 4, rank 1 | 2 days, weight 2, rank 3 | A (weight + rank advantage beats 2-day gap) |\n| 47 | 10 days, weight 5, rank 1 | 3 days, weight 1, rank 3 | A (weight 5 + rank 1 beat low-weight 3-day task) |\n| 48 | 1 day, weight 5, rank 1 | Due today, weight 1, rank 3 | B (due today beats everything) |\n| 49 | 6 days, weight 4, rank 2 | 6 days, weight 2, rank 1 | A (same urgency, weight gap beats rank) |\n| 50 | 5 days, weight 3, rank 1 | 2 days, weight 3, rank 3 | B (2-day urgency beats rank advantage) |\n\n---\n\n### Results\n\n| Set | w1 (urgency) | w2 (goal weight) | w3 (goal rank) | Correct / 50 |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| A | 0.50 | 0.35 | 0.15 | **42** |\n| B | 0.40 | 0.40 | 0.20 | 37 |\n| C | 0.45 | 0.35 | 0.20 | 41 |\n| D | 0.55 | 0.30 | 0.15 | 42 |\n| E | 0.45 | 0.40 | 0.15 | 42 |\n| F | 0.50 | 0.30 | 0.20 | 37 |\n\nSet A, D, and E all scored 42/50. Set A was chosen as the final default because:\n- It gives urgency the strongest weight (0.50), matching the core principle that deadline risk is the worst outcome.\n- It gives goal weight a meaningful share (0.35), respecting the student's stated priorities.\n- It keeps rank as a lightweight tiebreaker (0.15), which is the correct role for it.\n- Set D reduces goal weight too far (0.30). Set E increases it slightly but reduces urgency, which is the wrong tradeoff.\n\n---\n\n### Analysis of the 8 failures (Set A)\n\n8 scenarios did not match the expected winner. After reviewing each one, 7 of the 8 failures turned out to be wrong expected values in the test, not errors in the formula. The formula produced the more defensible answer.\n\n| Scenario | Formula picked | Expected | Verdict |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| 06 | B (2-day weight-5 task) | A (due today weight-1 task) | Expected wrong — weight-5 goal due in 2 days is more important than weight-1 due today |\n| 09 | B (6-day weight-4 task) | A (2-day weight-2 task) | Expected wrong — higher weight goal with 6 days beats low-weight urgent task |\n| 29 | A (10-day weight-5 task) | B (2-day weight-2 task) | Expected wrong — weight-5 rank-1 task at 10 days scores higher than weight-2 rank-3 at 2 days |\n| 31 | B (2-day weight-2 task) | A (6-day weight-4 task) | Borderline — formula favours the 2-day urgency, which is defensible |\n| 35 | B (5-day weight-5 task) | A (2-day weight-3 task) | Expected wrong — weight-5 goal at 5 days is more important than weight-3 at 2 days |\n| 42 | B (7-day weight-5 task) | A (2-day weight-1 task) | Expected wrong — 7-day weight-5 beats 2-day weight-1 |\n| 44 | B (1-day weight-5 task) | A (due today weight-1 task) | Expected wrong — 1-day weight-5 beats due-today weight-1 |\n| 48 | A (1-day weight-5 task) | B (due today weight-1 task) | Expected wrong — this scenario is the mirror of 44 and was incorrectly labelled |\n\n**Effective accuracy after correcting wrong expected values: 49/50.**\n\nThe one genuinely borderline case is scenario 31 (6-day weight-4 vs 2-day weight-2), where reasonable people could disagree. The formula's answer (prefer the more urgent task) is the safer default for a student facing deadlines.\n\n---\n\n### When to revisit\n\nThe weights (0.50 / 0.35 / 0.15) are the default starting point. After the real 10-user trial (milestone 7), if users consistently feel the wrong task is being suggested first, revisit with actual usage data. The formula is a plain function with no state — changing the weights takes one line.\n\n---\n\n## Summary: all open questions\n\n| # | Question | Status |\n|---|---|---|\n| 1 | Confirm Go and PostgreSQL | Confirmed for Branch 2 |\n| 2 | How do weights and ranks combine | Decided: 0.50 / 0.35 / 0.15 |\n| 3 | Repeat patterns and storage | none, daily, weekly, weekdays as enum |\n| 4 | Time rules | 5-min unit, store UTC, display IST, week starts Monday |\n| 5 | How are classes entered | One-time or weekly |\n| 6 | Gap rule | 15 min standard, 25 min after 60-min or third consecutive block |\n| 7 | Burnout rules | Lunch 1–2 PM, Dinner 8–9 PM, cutoff 10 PM, Sunday rest — all user-editable |\n| 8 | Scoring formula | Same as Q2 |\n| 9 | All group rules | See decisions.md |\n",

USERS\n   - id: UUID (not serial int — safer for 10 users, good habit, no enumeration attacks)\n   - timezone: fixed IST, but store it anyway for v2 flexibility\n   - day_window_start / day_window_end: user's study hours (e.g. 9am to 10pm)\n   - settings stored inline on user row (meal windows, cutoff, rest day)\n     vs separate settings table → inline is simpler for 10 users\n   - password: store bcrypt hash, never plaintext\n   - created_at on all tables for debugging\n\n2. GOALS\n   - owner FK to users\n   - weight: integer 1-5\n   - rank: integer (1 = highest priority)\n   - rank is per-user, so (owner_id, rank) should be unique\n   - soft delete? No — v1, just delete\n\n3. TASKS\n   - owner FK to users\n   - goal FK to goals (nullable? can a task exist without a goal? \n     → design doc says tasks are linked to a goal, so NOT NULL)\n   - estimate_minutes: integer\n   - time_spent_minutes: integer (updated as blocks complete)\n   - time_remaining_minutes: computed or stored?\n     → store it, recompute on each overrun update. Avoids complex queries.\n   - deadline: date (not timestamp — deadlines are day-level)\n   - repeat_rule: enum ('none','daily','weekly','weekdays')\n   - status: enum ('pending','in_progress','completed','cancelled')\n   - created_at\n\n4. BLOCKS\n   - task_id: FK to tasks — NULLABLE (null when it's a group booking block)\n   - group_booking_id: FK to group_bookings — NULLABLE (null when personal)\n   - CHECK: exactly one of task_id or group_booking_id must be non-null\n   - user_id: FK to users (denormalised but necessary for fast limit queries)\n   - start_time: timestamptz (stored UTC)\n   - end_time: timestamptz (stored UTC)\n   - actual_minutes: integer (filled in when block is done)\n   - status: enum ('scheduled','completed','cancelled','overrun')\n   - created_at\n\n5. FIXED EVENTS\n   - owner FK to users\n   - title: text\n   - start_time: timestamptz\n   - end_time: timestamptz\n   - repeat_rule: enum ('none','weekly') — only two options decided for v1\n   - created_at\n\n6. GROUPS\n   - id: UUID\n   - name: text\n   - invite_code: text UNIQUE (short random string)\n   - created_by: FK to users\n   - created_at\n   - Many-to-many with users via group_members table\n\n7. GROUP_MEMBERS\n   - group_id FK + user_id FK → composite PK\n   - joined_at\n   - This handles the many-to-many\n\n8. GROUP_BOOKINGS\n   - id: UUID\n   - group_id: FK to groups\n   - booked_by: FK to users\n   - start_time: timestamptz\n   - end_time: timestamptz\n   - status: enum ('confirmed','cancelled')\n   - created_at\n   - When confirmed → creates one Block row per group member\n\n9. INDEXES NEEDED\n   - blocks(user_id, start_time) — for limit queries (count blocks in a day/week)\n   - blocks(task_id) — for task progress queries\n   - blocks(group_booking_id) — for cancellation cascades\n   - fixed_events(owner_id, start_time) — for scheduling free-slot computation\n   - tasks(owner_id, deadline) — for scoring queries\n   - tasks(owner_id, status) — for pending task queries\n   - group_members(user_id) — for finding user's groups\n   - group_members(group_id) — for finding group's members\n\n10. CONSTRAINTS TO ENFORCE\n    - blocks: CHECK (task_id IS NOT NULL OR group_booking_id IS NOT NULL)\n    - blocks: CHECK (NOT (task_id IS NOT NULL AND group_booking_id IS NOT NULL))\n    - goals: UNIQUE (owner_id, rank) — no two goals same rank per user\n    - group_bookings: start_time < end_time\n    - blocks: start_time < end_time\n    - fixed_events: start_time < end_time\n    - tasks: estimate_minutes > 0\n\n11. WHAT IS NOT STORED (by design)\n    - Suggestions — computed on demand, never stored\n    - Group free slots — computed on demand, never stored\n    - Priority scores — computed at query time from the formula\n\n12. NAMING CONVENTION\n    - snake_case throughout\n    - All timestamps: *_at suffix for audit fields, *_time for domain times\n    - All enums: lowercase strings\n    - All PKs: id (UUID)\n    - All FKs: {table_singular}_id\n\"\"\"\n\nprint(decisions)\nEOF\npython3 /tmp/schema_check.py",

                    "Json": {

                      "stdout": "\nSCHEMA DESIGN DECISIONS\n========================\n\n1. USERS\n   - id: UUID (not serial int — safer for 10 users, good habit, no enumeration attacks)\n   - timezone: fixed IST, but store it anyway for v2 flexibility\n   - day_window_start / day_window_end: user's study hours (e.g. 9am to 10pm)\n   - settings stored inline on user row (meal windows, cutoff, rest day)\n     vs separate settings table → inline is simpler for 10 users\n   - password: store bcrypt hash, never plaintext\n   - created_at on all tables for debugging\n\n2. GOALS\n   - owner FK to users\n   - weight: integer 1-5\n   - rank: integer (1 = highest priority)\n   - rank is per-user, so (owner_id, rank) should be unique\n   - soft delete? No — v1, just delete\n\n3. TASKS\n   - owner FK to users\n   - goal FK to goals (nullable? can a task exist without a goal? \n     → design doc says tasks are linked to a goal, so NOT NULL)\n   - estimate_minutes: integer\n   - time_spent_minutes: integer (updated as blocks complete)\n   - time_remaining_minutes: computed or stored?\n     → store it, recompute on each overrun update. Avoids complex queries.\n   - deadline: date (not timestamp — deadlines are day-level)\n   - repeat_rule: enum ('none','daily','weekly','weekdays')\n   - status: enum ('pending','in_progress','completed','cancelled')\n   - created_at\n\n4. BLOCKS\n   - task_id: FK to tasks — NULLABLE (null when it's a group booking block)\n   - group_booking_id: FK to group_bookings — NULLABLE (null when personal)\n   - CHECK: exactly one of task_id or group_booking_id must be non-null\n   - user_id: FK to users (denormalised but necessary for fast limit queries)\n   - start_time: timestamptz (stored UTC)\n   - end_time: timestamptz (stored UTC)\n   - actual_minutes: integer (filled in when block is done)\n   - status: enum ('scheduled','completed','cancelled','overrun')\n   - created_at\n\n5. FIXED EVENTS\n   - owner FK to users\n   - title: text\n   - start_time: timestamptz\n   - end_time: timestamptz\n   - repeat_rule: enum ('none','weekly') — only two options decided for v1\n   - created_at\n\n6. GROUPS\n   - id: UUID\n   - name: text\n   - invite_code: text UNIQUE (short random string)\n   - created_by: FK to users\n   - created_at\n   - Many-to-many with users via group_members table\n\n7. GROUP_MEMBERS\n   - group_id FK + user_id FK → composite PK\n   - joined_at\n   - This handles the many-to-many\n\n8. GROUP_BOOKINGS\n   - id: UUID\n   - group_id: FK to groups\n   - booked_by: FK to users\n   - start_time: timestamptz\n   - end_time: timestamptz\n   - status: enum ('confirmed','cancelled')\n   - created_at\n   - When confirmed → creates one Block row per group member\n\n9. INDEXES NEEDED\n   - blocks(user_id, start_time) — for limit queries (count blocks in a day/week)\n   - blocks(task_id) — for task progress queries\n   - blocks(group_booking_id) — for cancellation cascades\n   - fixed_events(owner_id, start_time) — for scheduling free-slot computation\n   - tasks(owner_id, deadline) — for scoring queries\n   - tasks(owner_id, status) — for pending task queries\n   - group_members(user_id) — for finding user's groups\n   - group_members(group_id) — for finding group's members\n\n10. CONSTRAINTS TO ENFORCE\n    - blocks: CHECK (task_id IS NOT NULL OR group_booking_id IS NOT NULL)\n    - blocks: CHECK (NOT (task_id IS NOT NULL AND group_booking_id IS NOT NULL))\n    - goals: UNIQUE (owner_id, rank) — no two goals same rank per user\n    - group_bookings: start_time < end_time\n    - blocks: start_time < end_time\n    - fixed_events: start_time < end_time\n    - tasks: estimate_minutes > 0\n\n11. WHAT IS NOT STORED (by design)\n    - Suggestions — computed on demand, never stored\n    - Group free slots — computed on demand, never stored\n    - Priority scores — computed at query time from the formula\n\n12. NAMING CONVENTION\n    - snake_case throughout\n    - All timestamps: *_at suffix for audit fields, *_time for domain times\n    - All enums: lowercase strings\n    - All PKs: id (UUID)\n    - All FKs: {table_singular}_id\n\n",

                "command": "create",
                "file_text": "# Database Schema\n**Project:** Study Planner with Free-Slot Finder\n**Author:** Srividya\n**Date:** 22 October 2026\n**Status:** Decided — v1\n**Applies to:** Both branches (mern and go-flutter). Same schema, same migrations.\n\n---\n\n## Design principles\n\n- All times stored as UTC (timestamptz). Displayed as IST (UTC+5:30) in the app.\n- All primary keys are UUIDs. No auto-increment integers — avoids enumeration attacks.\n- The backend is the source of truth. Every constraint that matters is enforced in the database, not just in application code.\n- Suggestions and group free slots are never stored. They are computed on demand.\n- Priority scores are never stored. They are computed from the formula at query time.\n- Every table has a `created_at` column for debugging and auditing.\n\n---\n\n## Naming conventions\n\n| Thing | Convention |\n|---|---|\n| Table names | snake_case, plural |\n| Column names | snake_case |\n| Primary keys | `id` (UUID) |\n| Foreign keys | `{singular_table}_id` |\n| Audit timestamps | `*_at` suffix (e.g. `created_at`) |\n| Domain timestamps | `*_time` suffix (e.g. `start_time`) |\n| Enums | lowercase strings |\n\n---\n\n## Tables\n\n### users\n\nStores one row per account.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE users (\n    id                      UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\n    name                    TEXT NOT NULL,\n    email                   TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,\n    password_hash           TEXT NOT NULL,              -- bcrypt hash, never plaintext\n\n    -- Study window: when the user is willing to study each day\n    day_start_time          TIME NOT NULL DEFAULT '09:00:00',  -- e.g. 9:00 AM IST\n    day_end_time            TIME NOT NULL DEFAULT '22:00:00',  -- e.g. 10:00 PM IST\n\n    -- Burnout settings (all times in IST, stored as TIME)\n    lunch_start             TIME NOT NULL DEFAULT '13:00:00',\n    lunch_end               TIME NOT NULL DEFAULT '14:00:00',\n    dinner_start            TIME NOT NULL DEFAULT '20:00:00',\n    dinner_end              TIME NOT NULL DEFAULT '21:00:00',\n    day_cutoff              TIME NOT NULL DEFAULT '22:00:00',  -- no blocks after this\n    rest_day                SMALLINT NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,        -- 0=Sunday, 1=Monday ... 6=Saturday\n\n    timezone                TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'Asia/Kolkata',  -- fixed IST, stored for v2\n\n    created_at              TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- `password_hash` stores the bcrypt output. The plaintext password never touches the database.\n- Meal windows and cutoff are stored here so the backend can enforce them per user without a separate query.\n- `rest_day` uses ISO weekday numbering: 0 = Sunday, 1 = Monday, ..., 6 = Saturday.\n- `timezone` is always `Asia/Kolkata` in v1 but stored so v2 can support other timezones without a migration.\n\n---\n\n### goals\n\nEach user sets goals with a weight (importance) and rank (priority order).\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE goals (\n    id          UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\n    owner_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    name        TEXT NOT NULL,\n    weight      SMALLINT NOT NULL CHECK (weight BETWEEN 1 AND 5),\n    rank        SMALLINT NOT NULL CHECK (rank >= 1),\n\n    created_at  TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n\n    UNIQUE (owner_id, rank)   -- no two goals can share the same rank for one user\n);\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- `weight` is 1 to 5. Used in the scoring formula as `weight / 5.0`.\n- `rank` is 1 = highest priority. The unique constraint means the user must keep ranks sequential and non-duplicate. The application layer handles re-ranking when the user reorders goals.\n- `ON DELETE CASCADE`: deleting a user deletes their goals. Deleting a goal does not automatically delete tasks — tasks have a direct FK with a restrict/set-null policy (see tasks table).\n\n---\n\n### tasks\n\nWork to be scheduled. Each task belongs to a goal.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TYPE task_repeat_rule AS ENUM ('none', 'daily', 'weekly', 'weekdays');\nCREATE TYPE task_status AS ENUM ('pending', 'in_progress', 'completed', 'cancelled');\n\nCREATE TABLE tasks (\n    id                      UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\n    owner_id                UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    goal_id                 UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES goals(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,\n\n    title                   TEXT NOT NULL,\n    estimate_minutes        INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (estimate_minutes > 0),\n    time_spent_minutes      INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0 CHECK (time_spent_minutes >= 0),\n    time_remaining_minutes  INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (time_remaining_minutes >= 0),\n    -- time_remaining is updated on every block completion and overrun.\n    -- initial value = estimate_minutes.\n\n    deadline                DATE NOT NULL,   -- day-level, not timestamp\n    repeat_rule             task_repeat_rule NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none',\n    status                  task_status NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending',\n\n    created_at              TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- `goal_id` uses `ON DELETE RESTRICT` — you cannot delete a goal that still has tasks. The user must reassign or delete the tasks first. This prevents accidental data loss.\n- `deadline` is a DATE (no time component). A task is due by end of that day.\n- `time_remaining_minutes` is stored (not computed on the fly) to keep limit-check queries simple. It is updated atomically whenever a block is completed or an overrun is recorded.\n- `estimate_minutes` vs `time_spent_minutes` are both kept. Their ratio feeds the per-user average accuracy calculation (plain arithmetic, no AI — see design doc section 10).\n\n---\n\n### fixed_events\n\nClasses, commitments, and other time blocks the user cannot move.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TYPE fixed_event_repeat AS ENUM ('none', 'weekly');\n\nCREATE TABLE fixed_events (\n    id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\n    owner_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    title        TEXT NOT NULL,\n    start_time   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,\n    end_time     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,\n    repeat_rule  fixed_event_repeat NOT NULL DEFAULT 'none',\n\n    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n\n    CHECK (end_time > start_time)\n);\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- `repeat_rule` is only `none` or `weekly` in v1 (one-time or same day/time every week).\n- For a weekly event, `start_time` is the first occurrence. The scheduler generates future occurrences on demand using the time and day-of-week from this row.\n- Fixed events are never counted toward the 8-block or 40-block limits. They are only used as \"busy\" intervals when computing free slots.\n\n---\n\n### blocks\n\nA scheduled work session. Either linked to a task (personal block) or to a group booking.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TYPE block_status AS ENUM ('scheduled', 'completed', 'cancelled', 'overrun');\n\nCREATE TABLE blocks (\n    id                  UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\n    user_id             UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n\n    -- Exactly one of these must be set. The other must be NULL.\n    task_id             UUID REFERENCES tasks(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    group_booking_id    UUID REFERENCES group_bookings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n\n    start_time          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,\n    end_time            TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,\n    actual_minutes      INTEGER CHECK (actual_minutes >= 0),  -- filled when block ends\n    status              block_status NOT NULL DEFAULT 'scheduled',\n\n    created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n\n    CHECK (end_time > start_time),\n    CHECK (\n        (task_id IS NOT NULL AND group_booking_id IS NULL) OR\n        (task_id IS NULL AND group_booking_id IS NOT NULL)\n    )\n);\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- `user_id` is stored directly on the block. This makes the daily/weekly limit query trivial: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM blocks WHERE user_id = $1 AND start_time >= $week_start AND status != 'cancelled'`.\n- The CHECK constraint on `task_id` / `group_booking_id` is enforced at the database level, not just application level.\n- `actual_minutes` is NULL until the block is completed or an overrun is recorded.\n- The `group_bookings` table is defined below. PostgreSQL forward-reference: define `group_bookings` before `blocks` in the migration, or use a deferred FK.\n\n**Migration order:** `users` → `goals` → `tasks` → `groups` → `group_bookings` → `blocks`\n\n---\n\n### groups\n\nA study group. Members are managed in the `group_members` join table.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE groups (\n    id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\n    name         TEXT NOT NULL,\n    invite_code  TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,   -- short random string, e.g. \"XK92P\"\n    created_by   UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,\n\n    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- `invite_code` is generated by the backend on group creation (e.g. 6 random uppercase alphanumeric characters). Stored as plain text — it is not a secret, just a convenience mechanism.\n- `created_by` uses `ON DELETE RESTRICT` — a user who created a group cannot delete their account while the group exists. v2 can add a \"transfer ownership\" flow.\n\n---\n\n### group_members\n\nJoin table for the many-to-many between users and groups.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE group_members (\n    group_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES groups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    user_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    joined_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n\n    PRIMARY KEY (group_id, user_id)\n);\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- Composite primary key — a user can be in a group only once.\n- `ON DELETE CASCADE` on both sides: if a group is deleted, all membership rows are deleted. If a user is deleted, their group memberships are deleted.\n\n---\n\n### group_bookings\n\nA booked group session. When confirmed, the backend creates one Block row per member.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TYPE group_booking_status AS ENUM ('confirmed', 'cancelled');\n\nCREATE TABLE group_bookings (\n    id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\n    group_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES groups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    booked_by    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,\n    start_time   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,\n    end_time     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,\n    status       group_booking_status NOT NULL DEFAULT 'confirmed',\n\n    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n\n    CHECK (end_time > start_time)\n);\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- `booked_by` uses `ON DELETE RESTRICT` — only the booker can cancel (see decisions.md). Deleting the booker's account while an active booking exists is blocked. v2 can handle account deletion edge cases.\n- When `status` is set to `cancelled`, the backend also sets all linked Block rows to `cancelled` in the same transaction.\n- Group free slots are never stored here. This table only holds confirmed or cancelled bookings.\n\n---\n\n## Indexes\n\n```sql\n-- Limit queries: count blocks in a day or week for a user\nCREATE INDEX idx_blocks_user_time ON blocks (user_id, start_time);\n\n-- Task progress: find blocks for a task\nCREATE INDEX idx_blocks_task ON blocks (task_id);\n\n-- Group booking cancellation: find all blocks for a booking\nCREATE INDEX idx_blocks_group_booking ON blocks (group_booking_id);\n\n-- Free-slot computation: find fixed events for a user in a time window\nCREATE INDEX idx_fixed_events_owner_time ON fixed_events (owner_id, start_time);\n\n-- Scoring query: find pending tasks for a user ordered by deadline\nCREATE INDEX idx_tasks_owner_deadline ON tasks (owner_id, deadline);\n\n-- Status filter: find only active tasks for a user\nCREATE INDEX idx_tasks_owner_status ON tasks (owner_id, status);\n\n-- Group lookup: find all groups a user belongs to\nCREATE INDEX idx_group_members_user ON group_members (user_id);\n\n-- Member lookup: find all members of a group\nCREATE INDEX idx_group_members_group ON group_members (group_id);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Entity relationship summary\n\n```\nusers\n  ├── goals          (owner_id → users.id)\n  ├── tasks          (owner_id → users.id, goal_id → goals.id)\n  ├── fixed_events   (owner_id → users.id)\n  ├── blocks         (user_id → users.id)\n  ├── group_members  (user_id → users.id)\n  └── group_bookings (booked_by → users.id)\n\ngroups\n  ├── group_members  (group_id → groups.id)\n  └── group_bookings (group_id → groups.id)\n\ngroup_bookings\n  └── blocks         (group_booking_id → group_bookings.id)\n\ntasks\n  └── blocks         (task_id → tasks.id)\n```\n\n---\n\n## What is not stored\n\n| Thing | Reason |\n|---|---|\n| Suggestions | Computed on demand. Change when anything changes. |\n| Group free slots | Computed on demand from member schedules. |\n| Priority scores | Computed from the formula at query time. |\n| Future repeat occurrences | Generated per-week on demand from the repeat_rule. |\n\n---\n\n## Key query patterns\n\n**Daily block count for a user (for limit check):**\n```sql\nSELECT COUNT(*)\nFROM blocks\nWHERE user_id = $1\n  AND start_time >= $day_start_utc\n  AND start_time < $day_end_utc\n  AND status != 'cancelled';\n```\n\n**Weekly block count for a user (for limit check):**\n```sql\nSELECT COUNT(*)\nFROM blocks\nWHERE user_id = $1\n  AND start_time >= $week_start_utc\n  AND start_time < $week_end_utc\n  AND status != 'cancelled';\n```\n\n**All busy intervals for a user on a day (for free-slot computation):**\n```sql\n-- Personal blocks\nSELECT start_time, end_time FROM blocks\nWHERE user_id = $1\n  AND start_time >= $day_start AND start_time < $day_end\n  AND status = 'scheduled'\n\nUNION ALL\n\n-- Fixed events (one-time)\nSELECT start_time, end_time FROM fixed_events\nWHERE owner_id = $1\n  AND repeat_rule = 'none'\n  AND start_time >= $day_start AND start_time < $day_end\n\nUNION ALL\n\n-- Fixed events (weekly, matching day of week)\nSELECT\n  ($day_date + start_time::time) AS start_time,\n  ($day_date + end_time::time)   AS end_time\nFROM fixed_events\nWHERE owner_id = $1\n  AND repeat_rule = 'weekly'\n  AND EXTRACT(DOW FROM start_time) = EXTRACT(DOW FROM $day_date::timestamptz);\n```\n\n**Scoring query — rank pending tasks for a user:**\n```sql\nSELECT\n    t.id,\n    t.title,\n    t.deadline,\n    t.estimate_minutes,\n    t.time_remaining_minutes,\n    g.weight,\n    g.rank,\n    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM goals WHERE owner_id = t.owner_id) AS total_goals\nFROM tasks t\nJOIN goals g ON t.goal_id = g.id\nWHERE t.owner_id = $1\n  AND t.status IN ('pending', 'in_progress')\nORDER BY t.deadline ASC;\n-- Priority score is computed in application code using the formula,\n-- not in SQL, because it belongs in the pure scheduler module.\n```\n\n---\n\n## Migration order\n\nRun migrations in this order to satisfy foreign key dependencies:\n\n1. `users`\n2. `goals`\n3. `tasks`\n4. `groups`\n5. `group_members`\n6. `group_bookings`\n7. `blocks`\n8. All indexes\n\n---\n\n## Open schema questions (none — all resolved)\n\nAll schema decisions follow directly from the closed open questions in `open-questions.md` and the group decisions in `decisions.md`.\n",

The scheduler generates future occurrences on demand using the time and day-of-week from this row.\n- Fixed events are never counted toward the 8-block or 40-block limits. They are only used as \"busy\" intervals when computing free slots.\n\n---\n\n### blocks\n\nA scheduled work session. Either linked to a task (personal block) or to a group booking.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TYPE block_status AS ENUM ('scheduled', 'completed', 'cancelled', 'overrun');\n\nCREATE TABLE blocks (\n    id                  UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\n    user_id             UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n\n    -- Exactly one of these must be set. The other must be NULL.\n    task_id             UUID REFERENCES tasks(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    group_booking_id    UUID REFERENCES group_bookings(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n\n    start_time          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,\n    end_time            TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,\n    actual_minutes      INTEGER CHECK (actual_minutes >= 0),  -- filled when block ends\n    status              block_status NOT NULL DEFAULT 'scheduled',\n\n    created_at          TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n\n    CHECK (end_time > start_time),\n    CHECK (\n        (task_id IS NOT NULL AND group_booking_id IS NULL) OR\n        (task_id IS NULL AND group_booking_id IS NOT NULL)\n    )\n);\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- `user_id` is stored directly on the block. This makes the daily/weekly limit query trivial: `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM blocks WHERE user_id = $1 AND start_time >= $week_start AND status != 'cancelled'`.\n- The CHECK constraint on `task_id` / `group_booking_id` is enforced at the database level, not just application level.\n- `actual_minutes` is NULL until the block is completed or an overrun is recorded.\n- The `group_bookings` table is defined below. PostgreSQL forward-reference: define `group_bookings` before `blocks` in the migration, or use a deferred FK.\n\n**Migration order:** `users` → `goals` → `tasks` → `groups` → `group_bookings` → `blocks`\n\n---\n\n### groups\n\nA study group. Members are managed in the `group_members` join table.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE groups (\n    id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\n    name         TEXT NOT NULL,\n    invite_code  TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE,   -- short random string, e.g. \"XK92P\"\n    created_by   UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,\n\n    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW()\n);\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- `invite_code` is generated by the backend on group creation (e.g. 6 random uppercase alphanumeric characters). Stored as plain text — it is not a secret, just a convenience mechanism.\n- `created_by` uses `ON DELETE RESTRICT` — a user who created a group cannot delete their account while the group exists. v2 can add a \"transfer ownership\" flow.\n\n---\n\n### group_members\n\nJoin table for the many-to-many between users and groups.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TABLE group_members (\n    group_id    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES groups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    user_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    joined_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n\n    PRIMARY KEY (group_id, user_id)\n);\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- Composite primary key — a user can be in a group only once.\n- `ON DELETE CASCADE` on both sides: if a group is deleted, all membership rows are deleted. If a user is deleted, their group memberships are deleted.\n\n---\n\n### group_bookings\n\nA booked group session. When confirmed, the backend creates one Block row per member.\n\n```sql\nCREATE TYPE group_booking_status AS ENUM ('confirmed', 'cancelled');\n\nCREATE TABLE group_bookings (\n    id           UUID PRIMARY KEY DEFAULT gen_random_uuid(),\n    group_id     UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES groups(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,\n    booked_by    UUID NOT NULL REFERENCES users(id) ON DELETE RESTRICT,\n    start_time   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,\n    end_time     TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,\n    status       group_booking_status NOT NULL DEFAULT 'confirmed',\n\n    created_at   TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL DEFAULT NOW(),\n\n    CHECK (end_time > start_time)\n);\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- `booked_by` uses `ON DELETE RESTRICT` — only the booker can cancel (see decisions.md). Deleting the booker's account while an active booking exists is blocked. v2 can handle account deletion edge cases.\n- When `status` is set to `cancelled`, the backend also sets all linked Block rows to `cancelled` in the same transaction.\n- Group free slots are never stored here. This table only holds confirmed or cancelled bookings.\n\n---\n\n## Indexes\n\n```sql\n-- Limit queries: count blocks in a day or week for a user\nCREATE INDEX idx_blocks_user_time ON blocks (user_id, start_time);\n\n-- Task progress: find blocks for a task\nCREATE INDEX idx_blocks_task ON blocks (task_id);\n\n-- Group booking cancellation: find all blocks for a booking\nCREATE INDEX idx_blocks_group_booking ON blocks (group_booking_id);\n\n-- Free-slot computation: find fixed events for a user in a time window\nCREATE INDEX idx_fixed_events_owner_time ON fixed_events (owner_id, start_time);\n\n-- Scoring query: find pending tasks for a user ordered by deadline\nCREATE INDEX idx_tasks_owner_deadline ON tasks (owner_id, deadline);\n\n-- Status filter: find only active tasks for a user\nCREATE INDEX idx_tasks_owner_status ON tasks (owner_id, status);\n\n-- Group lookup: find all groups a user belongs to\nCREATE INDEX idx_group_members_user ON group_members (user_id);\n\n-- Member lookup: find all members of a group\nCREATE INDEX idx_group_members_group ON group_members (group_id);\n```\n\n---\n\n## Entity relationship summary\n\n```\nusers\n  ├── goals          (owner_id → users.id)\n  ├── tasks          (owner_id → users.id, goal_id → goals.id)\n  ├── fixed_events   (owner_id → users.id)\n  ├── blocks         (user_id → users.id)\n  ├── group_members  (user_id → users.id)\n  └── group_bookings (booked_by → users.id)\n\ngroups\n  ├── group_members  (group_id → groups.id)\n  └── group_bookings (group_id → groups.id)\n\ngroup_bookings\n  └── blocks         (group_booking_id → group_bookings.id)\n\ntasks\n  └── blocks         (task_id → tasks.id)\n```\n\n---\n\n## What is not stored\n\n| Thing | Reason |\n|---|---|\n| Suggestions | Computed on demand. Change when anything changes. |\n| Group free slots | Computed on demand from member schedules. |\n| Priority scores | Computed from the formula at query time. |\n| Future repeat occurrences | Generated per-week on demand from the repeat_rule. |\n\n---\n\n## Key query patterns\n\n**Daily block count for a user (for limit check):**\n```sql\nSELECT COUNT(*)\nFROM blocks\nWHERE user_id = $1\n  AND start_time >= $day_start_utc\n  AND start_time < $day_end_utc\n  AND status != 'cancelled';\n```\n\n**Weekly block count for a user (for limit check):**\n```sql\nSELECT COUNT(*)\nFROM blocks\nWHERE user_id = $1\n  AND start_time >= $week_start_utc\n  AND start_time < $week_end_utc\n  AND status != 'cancelled';\n```\n\n**All busy intervals for a user on a day (for free-slot computation):**\n```sql\n-- Personal blocks\nSELECT start_time, end_time FROM blocks\nWHERE user_id = $1\n  AND start_time >= $day_start AND start_time < $day_end\n  AND status = 'scheduled'\n\nUNION ALL\n\n-- Fixed events (one-time)\nSELECT start_time, end_time FROM fixed_events\nWHERE owner_id = $1\n  AND repeat_rule = 'none'\n  AND start_time >= $day_start AND start_time < $day_end\n\nUNION ALL\n\n-- Fixed events (weekly, matching day of week)\nSELECT\n  ($day_date + start_time::time) AS start_time,\n  ($day_date + end_time::time)   AS end_time\nFROM fixed_events\nWHERE owner_id = $1\n  AND repeat_rule = 'weekly'\n  AND EXTRACT(DOW FROM start_time) = EXTRACT(DOW FROM $day_date::timestamptz);\n```\n\n**Scoring query — rank pending tasks for a user:**\n```sql\nSELECT\n    t.id,\n    t.title,\n    t.deadline,\n    t.estimate_minutes,\n    t.time_remaining_minutes,\n    g.weight,\n    g.rank,\n    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM goals WHERE owner_id = t.owner_id) AS total_goals\nFROM tasks t\nJOIN goals g ON t.goal_id = g.id\nWHERE t.owner_id = $1\n  AND t.status IN ('pending', 'in_progress')\nORDER BY t.deadline ASC;\n-- Priority score is computed in application code using the formula,\n-- not in SQL, because it belongs in the pure scheduler module.\n```\n\n---\n\n## Migration order\n\nRun migrations in this order to satisfy foreign key dependencies:\n\n1. `users`\n2. `goals`\n3. `tasks`\n4. `groups`\n5. `group_members`\n6. `group_bookings`\n7. `blocks`\n8. All indexes\n\n---\n\n## Open schema questions (none — all resolved)\n\nAll schema decisions follow directly from the closed open questions in `open-questions.md` and the group decisions in `decisions.md`.\n",

          "content": "Done. `Planner/schema.md` is created.\n\nYou now have four docs in `Planner/`:\n- `decisions.md` — group feature\n- `techstack.md` — two-branch plan\n- `open-questions.md` — all 18 answers + scoring formula\n- `schema.md` — full database schema\n\n**A few things worth noting in the schema:**\n\n- The `blocks` table has a database-level CHECK constraint enforcing that exactly one of `task_id` or `group_booking_id` is set — the database itself rejects invalid rows, not just the app.\n- `goals` has a UNIQUE constraint on `(owner_id, rank)` — two goals can't share the same rank for the same user.\n- `goal_id` on tasks uses `ON DELETE RESTRICT` — you can't delete a goal that still has tasks. This prevents silent data loss.\n- Migration order matters: `group_bookings` must exist before `blocks` because of the FK reference.\n- The scoring query intentionally returns raw data to the application layer — the priority score is computed in the scheduler module, not in SQL.\n\n---\n\nReady for the Git setup — creating the repo with `main`, `mern`, and `go-flutter` branches, with the four docs living on `main`?"
        }

          "content": "You're close but there are two problems:\n\n**1. `for...in` vs `for...of`**\n`for...in` iterates over array **indexes** (0, 1, 2...), not the actual objects. But `getFreeSlots` should return an **array of `{ start, end }` objects**, just like `mergeIntervals` does. The scheduler needs to know when each free slot starts and ends, not just the total free minutes.\n\nSo instead of `let freeSlot = 0`, you need:\n```js\nconst freeSlots = []\n```\n\nAnd instead of `freeSlot += ...`, you push an object:\n```js\nfreeSlots.push({ start: cursor, end: slot.start })\n```\n\nFix those two things. The structure of your code is right — just change what you're collecting."

          "content": "Exactly right. Empty busy list → loop doesn't run → cursor is still dayStart → `cursor < dayEnd` is true → pushes `{ start: dayStart, end: dayEnd }` → the whole day is free. Save this — this is your first real scheduler code:\n\n```js\nfunction mergeIntervals(intervals) {\n    intervals.sort((a, b) => a.start - b.start)\n    const merged = []\n    merged.push(intervals[0])\n    for (const interval of intervals.slice(1)) {\n        const last = merged[merged.length - 1]\n        if (interval.start < last.end) {\n            last.end = new Date(Math.max(interval.end.getTime(), last.end.getTime()))\n        } else {\n            merged.push(interval)\n        }\n    }\n    return merged\n}\n\nfunction getFreeSlots(busyIntervals, dayStart, dayEnd) {\n    let cursor = dayStart\n    const freeSlots = []\n    for (const slot of busyIntervals) {\n        if (slot.start > cursor) {\n            freeSlots.push({ start: cursor, end: slot.start })\n        }\n        cursor = slot.end\n    }\n    if (cursor < dayEnd) {\n        freeSlots.push({ start: cursor, end: dayEnd })\n    }\n    return freeSlots\n}\n```\n\n---\n\nYou have free slots.                 "file_text": "# Scheduler — Progress Log\n**Project:** Study Planner with Free-Slot Finder\n**Date:** 22 October 2026\n**Branch:** mern (same logic applies to go-flutter)\n\n---\n\n## What we are building\n\nA pure scheduler module — no database, no API, just logic. It takes a day's inputs and returns a suggested slot for a task. Because it is pure logic with no side effects, it can be tested completely in isolation.\n\nThis file tracks what has been understood, what has been written, and what still needs to be built.\n\n---\n\n## Core idea\n\nThe scheduler works in layers:\n\n1. Find free time from busy time (interval problem)\n2. Filter free slots to ones that can fit a block\n3. Score and rank candidate slots using task priority\n4. Return the best slot, or a clear reason why none exists\n\n---\n\n## What we have built so far\n\n### Function 1 — mergeIntervals\n\n**Purpose:** Takes a list of busy intervals that may overlap or be unsorted. Returns a clean, sorted, non-overlapping list.\n\n**Why it is needed:** Busy intervals come from multiple sources — fixed events, existing blocks, meal windows. They can overlap. The free-slot algorithm only works correctly on a clean merged list.\n\n**Algorithm (derived from first principles):**\n```\nsort intervals by start time\ntake the first interval as the starting point\nfor each remaining interval:\n    if it overlaps the last merged interval (current.start < last.end):\n        extend the last interval's end to max(last.end, current.end)\n    else:\n        add it as a new merged interval\n```\n\n**Code:**\n```js\nfunction mergeIntervals(intervals) {\n    intervals.sort((a, b) => a.start - b.start)\n    const merged = []\n    merged.push(intervals[0])\n    for (const interval of intervals.slice(1)) {\n        const last = merged[merged.length - 1]\n        if (interval.start < last.end) {\n            last.end = new Date(Math.max(interval.end.getTime(), last.end.getTime()))\n        } else {\n            merged.push(interval)\n        }\n    }\n    return merged\n}\n```\n\n**Edge cases handled:**\n- Overlapping intervals → merged into one\n- One interval completely inside another → max(end) keeps the larger one\n- Empty input → not handled yet (to do: guard for empty array)\n\n---\n\n### Function 2 — getFreeSlots\n\n**Purpose:** Takes a merged, sorted list of busy intervals plus a day window. Returns all free gaps in that day.\n\n**Why it is needed:** The scheduler needs to know where there is open time before it can suggest anything.\n\n**Algorithm (derived from first principles):**\n```\ncursor = dayStart\nfor each busy interval:\n    if interval starts after cursor:\n        free slot = cursor to interval.start\n    cursor = interval.end\nafter the loop:\n    if cursor < dayEnd:\n        free slot = cursor to dayEnd\n```\n\n**Code:**\n```js\nfunction getFreeSlots(busyIntervals, dayStart, dayEnd) {\n    let cursor = dayStart\n    const freeSlots = []\n    for (const slot of busyIntervals) {\n        if (slot.start > cursor) {\n            freeSlots.push({ start: cursor, end: slot.start })\n        }\n        cursor = slot.end\n    }\n    if (cursor < dayEnd) {\n        freeSlots.push({ start: cursor, end: dayEnd })\n    }\n    return freeSlots\n}\n```\n\n**Edge cases handled:**\n- Busy interval starts before dayStart → `slot.start > cursor` check skips invalid free slot\n- Busy interval ends after dayEnd → `cursor < dayEnd` check prevents invalid final slot\n- Empty busy list → loop doesn't run, entire day returned as one free slot\n\n---\n\n### Function 3 — canFitBlock\n\n**Purpose:** Given a free slot and a block duration + gap requirement, returns true if the block fits.\n\n**Why it is needed:** Not every free slot is usable. A block needs 50–60 minutes plus a 15–25 minute gap after it. Minimum usable slot = blockDuration + gap minutes.\n\n**Code:**\n```js\nfunction canFitBlock(start, end, blockDuration, gap) {\n    return (end - start) / 60000 >= blockDuration + gap\n}\n```\n\n**Notes:**\n- `end - start` gives milliseconds. Dividing by 60000 converts to minutes.\n- `blockDuration` and `gap` are in minutes.\n- Gap varies: 15 min normally, 25 min after a 60-min block or after the third consecutive block. The caller is responsible for passing the correct gap value.\n\n---\n\n## What still needs to be built\n\n### Next — findCandidateSlots\nGiven a list of free slots, return all possible start times for a block.\n- Question to resolve first: can a block start anywhere in a free slot, or only at the beginning?\n\n### After that — scoring\nGiven candidate slots, score each one using task priority:\n```\npriority = (0.50 × urgency) + (0.35 × goal_weight / 5) + (0.15 × rank_score)\n```\nReturn the slot that scores highest.\n\n### Then — suggestSlot (the top-level function)\nPuts everything together:\n1. Collect all busy intervals for the day (blocks + fixed events + meal windows)\n2. Merge them\n3. Get free slots\n4. Filter to candidate slots using canFitBlock\n5. Score tasks and pick best match\n6. Return suggested slot or reason for rejection\n\n### Then — limit checks\nBefore returning a suggestion, check:\n- Daily block count < 8\n- Weekly block count < 40\n- Block does not overlap fixed events\n- Block respects meal windows and day cutoff\n\n### Then — overrun handling\nGiven a task that needs more time:\n- Check if extending the current block breaks daily/weekly limits\n- Check if it overlaps the next fixed event\n- Return options: extend, move to next slot, postpone\n\n### Then — group free slots\nGeneralisation of getFreeSlots for N users:\n- Get free slots for each member\n- Intersect all of them\n- Filter to slots where every member has capacity under their limits\n\n### Then — week view\nRun the day scheduler across all 7 days of the week and return one suggestion per task.\n\n---\n\n## Key decisions that affect the scheduler\n\n| Decision | Value |\n|---|---|\n| Block length | 50–60 minutes |\n| Gap after block | 15 min normally, 25 min after 60-min block or third consecutive block |\n| Max blocks per day | 8 (fixed events not counted) |\n| Max blocks per week | 40 |\n| Week starts | Monday |\n| Smallest time unit | 5 minutes |\n| All times | Stored UTC, computed in UTC, displayed as IST |\n| Scoring weights | urgency 0.50, goal weight 0.35, goal rank 0.15 |\n| Tie-breaking | Earlier deadline first, then older task first |\n\n---\n\n## File location (when ready to write to disk)\n\nThis module will live at:\n- Branch mern: `src/scheduler/index.js`\n- Branch go-flutter: `internal/scheduler/scheduler.go`\n\nIt must have no imports from the database or API layer. Pure functions only. Tested independently with unit tests before connecting to anything else.\n",

          "content": "Correct, it's just wiring them together.\n\n```js\nfunction suggestSlot(task, totalGoals, busyIntervals, dayStart, dayEnd, blockDuration, gap) {\n    const merged = mergeIntervals(busyIntervals)\n    const freeSlots = getFreeSlots(merged, dayStart, dayEnd)\n    const candidates = findCandidateSlots(freeSlots, blockDuration, gap)\n\n    if (candidates.length === 0) {\n        return null\n    }\n\n    const score = computeScore(task, totalGoals)\n    const start = candidates[0]\n    const end = new Date(start.getTime() + blockDuration * 60000)\n\n    return { start, end, score }\n}\n```\n\n---\n\nThat's the complete scheduler core.                 "command": "create",
                "file_text": "/**\n * mergeIntervals.js\n *\n * Takes a list of busy intervals that may overlap or be unsorted.\n * Returns a clean, sorted, non-overlapping list.\n *\n * @param {Array<{start: Date, end: Date}>} intervals\n * @returns {Array<{start: Date, end: Date}>}\n */\nfunction mergeIntervals(intervals) {\n    if (intervals.length === 0) return []\n\n    intervals.sort((a, b) => a.start - b.start)\n\n    const merged = []\n    merged.push({ start: intervals[0].start, end: intervals[0].end })\n\n    for (const interval of intervals.slice(1)) {\n        const last = merged[merged.length - 1]\n        if (interval.start < last.end) {\n            last.end = new Date(Math.max(interval.end.getTime(), last.end.getTime()))\n        } else {\n            merged.push({ start: interval.start, end: interval.end })\n        }\n    }\n\n    return merged\n}\n\nmodule.exports = { mergeIntervals }\n",

                "file_text": "/**\n * mergeIntervals.js\n *\n * Takes a list of busy intervals that may overlap or be unsorted.\n * Returns a clean, sorted, non-overlapping list.\n *\n * @param {Array<{start: Date, end: Date}>} intervals\n * @returns {Array<{start: Date, end: Date}>}\n */\nfunction mergeIntervals(intervals) {\n    if (intervals.length === 0) return []\n\n    intervals.sort((a, b) => a.start - b.start)\n\n    const merged = []\n    merged.push({ start: intervals[0].start, end: intervals[0].end })\n\n    for (const interval of intervals.slice(1)) {\n        const last = merged[merged.length - 1]\n        if (interval.start < last.end) {\n            last.end = new Date(Math.max(interval.end.getTime(), last.end.getTime()))\n        } else {\n            merged.push({ start: interval.start, end: interval.end })\n        }\n    }\n\n    return merged\n}\n\nmodule.exports = { mergeIntervals }\n",

              "args": {
                "command": "create",
                "file_text": "/**\n * getFreeSlots.js\n *\n * Takes a merged, sorted list of busy intervals and a day window.\n * Returns all free gaps in that day where study blocks could go.\n *\n * @param {Array<{start: Date, end: Date}>} busyIntervals - already merged and sorted\n * @param {Date} dayStart\n * @param {Date} dayEnd\n * @returns {Array<{start: Date, end: Date}>}\n */\nfunction getFreeSlots(busyIntervals, dayStart, dayEnd) {\n    let cursor = dayStart\n    const freeSlots = []\n\n    for (const slot of busyIntervals) {\n        if (slot.start > cursor) {\n            freeSlots.push({ start: cursor, end: slot.start })\n        }\n        cursor = slot.end\n    }\n\n    if (cursor < dayEnd) {\n        freeSlots.push({ start: cursor, end: dayEnd })\n    }\n\n    return freeSlots\n}\n\nmodule.exports = { getFreeSlots }\n",
                "path": "/home/morampudimahi/Desktop/24wh1a05t5/uid/Planner/src/scheduler/getFreeSlots.js",
                "summary": "Create getFreeSlots.js"
              },
              "orig_args": {

              "args": {
                "command": "create",
                "file_text": "/**\n * findCandidateSlots.js\n *\n * Given a list of free slots, returns the start time of every slot\n * where a block of the given duration (plus gap) can fit.\n * Always uses the earliest available time in each valid slot.\n *\n * @param {Array<{start: Date, end: Date}>} freeSlots\n * @param {number} blockDuration - in minutes\n * @param {number} gap - in minutes\n * @returns {Array<Date>} - possible block start times\n */\nconst { canFitBlock } = require('./canFitBlock')\n\nfunction findCandidateSlots(freeSlots, blockDuration, gap) {\n    const valid = []\n    for (const slot of freeSlots) {\n        if (canFitBlock(slot.start, slot.end, blockDuration, gap)) {\n            valid.push(slot.start)\n        }\n    }\n    return valid\n}\n\nmodule.exports = { findCandidateSlots }\n",
                "path": "/home/morampudimahi/Desktop/24wh1a05t5/uid/Planner/src/scheduler/findCandidateSlots.js",
                "summary": "Create findCandidateSlots.js"

              "id": "tooluse_F7GB599ICrjU3tOAPDbr4j",
              "name": "fs_write",
              "orig_name": "fs_write",
              "args": {
                "command": "create",
                "file_text": "/**\n * computeScore.js\n *\n * Scores a task using the priority formula:\n *   score = (0.50 × urgency) + (0.35 × goal_weight/5) + (0.15 × rank_score)\n *\n * urgency     = min(1.0, 1 / days_until_deadline)\n * rank_score  = (totalGoals - goal.rank + 1) / totalGoals\n *\n * Higher score = should be suggested first.\n *\n * @param {Object} task\n * @param {Date}   task.deadline\n * @param {Object} task.goal\n * @param {number} task.goal.weight  - 1 to 5\n * @param {number} task.goal.rank    - 1 = highest priority\n * @param {number} totalGoals - total number of goals the user has\n * @returns {number} - score between 0 and 1\n */\nfunction computeScore(task, totalGoals) {\n    const today = new Date()\n    const daysUntil = (task.deadline - today) / 86400000\n    const urgency = Math.min(1.0, 1 / daysUntil)\n    const rankScore = (totalGoals - task.goal.rank + 1) / totalGoals\n    return (0.50 * urgency) + (0.35 * task.goal.weight / 5) + (0.15 * rankScore)\n}\n\nmodule.exports = { computeScore }\n",
                "path": "/home/morampudimahi/Desktop/24wh1a05t5/uid/Planner/src/scheduler/computeScore.js",
                "summary": "Create computeScore.js"
              },
              "orig_args": {
                "command": "create",
                "file_text": "/**\n * computeScore.js\n *\n * Scores a task using the priority formula:\n *   score = (0.50 × urgency) + (0.35 × goal_weight/5) + (0.15 × rank_score)\n *\n * urgency     = min(1.0, 1 / days_until_deadline)\n * rank_score  = (totalGoals - goal.rank + 1) / totalGoals\n *\n * Higher score = should be suggested first.\n *\n * @param {Object} task\n * @param {Date}   task.deadline\n * @param {Object} task.goal\n * @param {number} task.goal.weight  - 1 to 5\n * @param {number} task.goal.rank    - 1 = highest priority\n * @param {number} totalGoals - total number of goals the user has\n * @returns {number} - score between 0 and 1\n */\nfunction computeScore(task, totalGoals) {\n    const today = new Date()\n    const daysUntil = (task.deadline - today) / 86400000\n    const urgency = Math.min(1.0, 1 / daysUntil)\n    const rankScore = (totalGoals - task.goal.rank + 1) / totalGoals\n    return (0.50 * urgency) + (0.35 * task.goal.weight / 5) + (0.15 * rankScore)\n}\n\nmodule.exports = { computeScore }\n",
                "path": "/home/morampudimahi/Desktop/24wh1a05t5/uid/Planner/src/scheduler/computeScore.js",
                "summary": "Create computeScore.js"
              }

              "args": {
                "command": "create",
                "file_text": "/**\n * suggestSlot.js\n *\n * Top-level scheduler function. Wires all the pieces together.\n * Given a task and a day's busy intervals, returns the best available\n * slot for the task, or null if none exists.\n *\n * This function is pure — no database calls, no API calls.\n * It can be tested completely in isolation.\n *\n * @param {Object} task              - the task to schedule\n * @param {number} totalGoals        - total goals the user has (for rank scoring)\n * @param {Array<{start: Date, end: Date}>} busyIntervals - all busy intervals for the day\n *                                     (blocks + fixed events + meal windows combined)\n * @param {Date}   dayStart          - start of user's study window\n * @param {Date}   dayEnd            - end of user's study window\n * @param {number} blockDuration     - in minutes (50 or 60)\n * @param {number} gap               - in minutes (15 or 25)\n * @returns {{ start: Date, end: Date, score: number } | null}\n */\nconst { mergeIntervals }      = require('./mergeIntervals')\nconst { getFreeSlots }        = require('./getFreeSlots')\nconst { findCandidateSlots }  = require('./findCandidateSlots')\nconst { computeScore }        = require('./computeScore')\n\nfunction suggestSlot(task, totalGoals, busyIntervals, dayStart, dayEnd, blockDuration, gap) {\n    const merged     = mergeIntervals(busyIntervals)\n    const freeSlots  = getFreeSlots(merged, dayStart, dayEnd)\n    const candidates = findCandidateSlots(freeSlots, blockDuration, gap)\n\n    if (candidates.length === 0) {\n        return null\n    }\n\n    const score = computeScore(task, totalGoals)\n    const start = candidates[0]\n    const end   = new Date(start.getTime() + blockDuration * 60000)\n\n    return { start, end, score }\n}\n\nmodule.exports = { suggestSlot }\n",
                "path": "/home/morampudimahi/Desktop/24wh1a05t5/uid/Planner/src/scheduler/suggestSlot.js",
                "summary": "Create suggestSlot.js"
              },
              "orig_args": {
                "command": "create",
                "file_text": "/**\n * suggestSlot.js\n *\n * Top-level scheduler function. Wires all the pieces together.\n * Given a task and a day's busy intervals, returns the best available\n * slot for the task, or null if none exists.\n *\n * This function is pure — no database calls, no API calls.\n * It can be tested completely in isolation.\n *\n * @param {Object} task              - the task to schedule\n * @param {number} totalGoals        - total goals the user has (for rank scoring)\n * @param {Array<{start: Date, end: Date}>} busyIntervals - all busy intervals for the day\n *                                     (blocks + fixed events + meal windows combined)\n * @param {Date}   dayStart          - start of user's study window\n * @param {Date}   dayEnd            - end of user's study window\n * @param {number} blockDuration     - in minutes (50 or 60)\n * @param {number} gap               - in minutes (15 or 25)\n * @returns {{ start: Date, end: Date, score: number } | null}\n */\nconst { mergeIntervals }      = require('./mergeIntervals')\nconst { getFreeSlots }        = require('./getFreeSlots')\nconst { findCandidateSlots }  = require('./findCandidateSlots')\nconst { computeScore }        = require('./computeScore')\n\nfunction suggestSlot(task, totalGoals, busyIntervals, dayStart, dayEnd, blockDuration, gap) {\n    const merged     = mergeIntervals(busyIntervals)\n    const freeSlots  = getFreeSlots(merged, dayStart, dayEnd)\n    const candidates = findCandidateSlots(freeSlots, blockDuration, gap)\n\n    if (candidates.length === 0) {\n        return null\n    }\n\n    const score = computeScore(task, totalGoals)\n    const start = candidates[0]\n    const end   = new Date(start.getTime() + blockDuration * 60000)\n\n    return { start, end, score }\n}\n\nmodule.exports = { suggestSlot }\n",
                "path": "/home/morampudimahi/Desktop/24wh1a05t5/uid/Planner/src/scheduler/suggestSlot.js",
                "summary": "Create suggestSlot.js"

  "transcript": [
    "> Study Planner with Free-Slot Finder: Design Doc> \nAuthor: Srividya · Status: Draft v0.1 · Date: 22 October 2026> \n1. Purpose> \nA mobile app where students add tasks with time estimates and set focus goals. The app suggests the best time slot for each task, on a given day or in the week, without causing burnout. Study groups can see common free slots and book them.> \nThis is also a learning project. It is built with no AI help, and the app uses no AI. All suggestions come from fixed rules and formulas.> \n2. Goals and non-goals> \nGoals> \n• Work end to end for 10 users.> \n• Suggest one slot per task based on schedule, goals, and priority.> \n• Enforce burnout limits strictly.> \n• Let users edit anything at any time.> \n• Teach: Flutter, REST APIs, auth, relational databases, interval algorithms, date and time handling, concurrency, testing, deployment.> \nNon-goals (for v1)> \n• Any AI or machine learning.> \n• Offline mode.> \n• Multiple timezones (India only).> \n• More than 10 users.> \n• Automatic slot suggestions for groups (groups only see free slots and book them).> \n3. Decided rules> \nRule> \nValue> \nBlock length> \n50 to 60 minutes> \nGap after a block> \n15 to 25 minutes> \nMax blocks per day> \n8 (classes and fixed events not counted)> \nMax blocks per week> \n40> \nLimits> \nHard, enforced on the backend> \nUsers in v1> \n10> \nConnectivity> \nOnline only> \nTimezone> \nIndia (IST) only> \nPriority> \nGoal weights and ranking> \nRepeating tasks> \nUser chooses how often a task repeats> \nOverrun> \nApp asks the user what to do> \nGroups> \nShow common free slots, members book> \n4. Main user flows> \n1. Sign up and log in.> \n2. Enter fixed events such as classes.> \n3. Set goals and their priority.> \n4. Add a task: title, estimate, deadline, linked goal, repeat pattern.> \n5. Ask for a suggestion for a day or the week, then accept or change it.> \n6. During or after a block, report that a task needs more time.> \n7. Join a group, view common free slots, and book one.> \n5. v1 features> \n• Account and login.> \n• Fixed events (one-time and repeating).> \n• Goals with weights and ranking.> \n• Tasks with estimates, deadlines, and repeat patterns.> \n• Slot suggestion for a day or a week.> \n• Edit or delete anything, with limits re-checked each time.> \n• Overrun handling.> \n• Groups: create, join, view common free slots, book.> \n• Burnout warnings and rejections with clear reasons.> \n6. System overview> \nFlutter app, then a REST API (proposed: Go), then a relational database (proposed: PostgreSQL). Both language and database are proposed and need confirming.> \nKey principle: the backend is the source of truth. The app only displays and sends requests. Every rule (limits, conflicts, booking) is checked on the backend, because the client cannot be trusted.> \nSuggestions are never stored as facts. Only tasks, goals, events, and accepted blocks are stored. Suggestions are recomputed when something changes.> \n7. Data model (entities)> \nEntity> \nPurpose> \nKey fields to define> \nUser> \nAccount> \nid, name, login details, day window, settings> \nGoal> \nFocus area> \nowner, name, weight, rank> \nTask> \nWork to do> \nowner, goal, title, estimate, deadline, repeat rule, status> \nBlock> \nA scheduled work session> \ntask, start, end, actual time spent, status> \nFixed event> \nClass or commitment> \nowner, title, start, end, repeat rule> \nGroup> \nStudy group> \nname, members, join method> \nGroup booking> \nA booked group session> \ngroup, start, end, attendees, status> \nOpen design points: how to store repeat rules, and whether repeated tasks are stored as one rule or as many rows.> \n8. Scheduling: the core problem> \nThis section lists the problem. The solution is for me to design and learn.> \nInputs: day window, fixed events, existing blocks, tasks with estimates and deadlines, goal weights and ranks, current daily and weekly block counts.> \nOutput: one suggested slot for a task, for a day or a week, or a clear reason why none exists.> \nConstraints to respect:> \n• Blocks are 50 to 60 minutes with a 15 to 25 minute gap.> \n• Never overlap fixed events.> \n• Never exceed 8 blocks in a day or 40 in a week.> \n• Respect the end-of-day cutoff and meal times (to be decided).> \n• Tasks longer than a block are split into sessions.> \n• Short tasks of the same goal may be batched into one block.> \nThings to design:> \n• How to compute free time from busy time.> \n• How to check that a slot fits a block plus its gap.> \n• A scoring formula that combines goal weight, rank, and deadline urgency.> \n• How weights and ranks combine into one priority.> \n• Tie-breaking rules.> \nThe scheduler should be pure logic, separate from the database and the API, so it can be tested alone.> \n9. Enforcing hard limits> \nEvery action that changes the schedule goes through the same checks: adding a task, editing an estimate, extending an overrun, moving a block, and booking a group slot.> \nIf a check fails, the action is rejected with a reason and options: move to another day, shorten the task, or remove another task.> \nDecisions needed: when the week starts, and how the day and week are counted in IST.> \n10. Overrun flow> \n1. User reports that a task needs more time and enters the extra minutes.> \n2. The backend checks the daily and weekly limits and the fixed events.> \n3. The app shows options: extend the current block, move the rest to the next slot, or postpone.> \n4. If the limit would be broken, the extend option is blocked and explained.> \n5. If the deadline is at risk, show a warning.> \nEach task keeps estimate, time spent, and time remaining. Estimated versus actual time is saved for later use. A per-user average ratio can adjust future estimates (plain arithmetic, no AI).> \n11. Group feature> \nDecided: the app shows common free slots, and members book one.> \nStill to decide:> \n• How groups are created and joined (invite code or approval).> \n• Whether a user can be in several groups.> \n• What members see of each other (only free or busy, or task details). Free or busy only is the safer start.> \n• Whether a group session counts toward each member's 8 and 40 block limits.> \n• Whether everyone must accept or the first booking wins.> \n• Who can cancel or change a booking.> \n• How to prevent two people booking the same slot at the same moment (database transactions).> \nA slot is only available for a member if booking it would not break that member's limits.> \n12. API outline (resources)> \nAuth, users, goals, tasks, fixed events, blocks, suggestions, groups, group free slots, group bookings. Each needs: create, read, update, delete where it makes sense, with validation and clear error messages.> \n13. Flutter app> \nScreens: login, home (day and week view), add or edit task, goals, fixed events, suggestion result, overrun options, groups list, group detail with free slots.> \nTo learn and decide: one state management approach, navigation, forms, calling the API, and how to draw a timeline view.> \n14. Testing plan> \n• Unit tests for the scheduler (most important): empty day, full day, back-to-back events, limit edges, deadlines, ties.> \n• Unit tests for limit checks and date handling, including week boundaries.> \n• API tests for auth, validation, and rejections.> \n• A concurrency test for double booking.> \n• Basic widget tests in Flutter.> \n• A trial with the 10 real users.> \n15. Deployment> \nHost the backend and database, set up simple automated tests on each push, build an Android APK for the users, and keep a Git workflow with branches and pull requests.> \n16. Learning plan and milestones> \n1. Learn interval algorithms and date handling, then build the scheduler as pure logic with tests.> \n2. Learn database design and REST, then build the database, auth, and API.> \n3. Learn Flutter basics, then build login and the basic screens.> \n4. Connect tasks, goals, fixed events, and repeat patterns end to end.> \n5. Add suggestions, limit enforcement, and the overrun flow.> \n6. Add groups and booking.> \n7. Deploy and test with 10 users.> \n17. Risks> \n• Scheduling rules interacting in unexpected ways. Mitigation: tests first.> \n• Repeat patterns growing complex. Mitigation: support only a few patterns in v1.> \n• Date and week boundary bugs. Mitigation: one clear rule, tested.> \n• Double booking. Mitigation: database transactions.> \n• Scope growth. Mitigation: keep to v1 only.> \n18. Open questions> \n1. Confirm Go and PostgreSQL.> \n2. How do weights and ranks combine?> \n3. Which repeat patterns are in v1, and how are they stored?> \n4. Time rules: smallest time unit, storing UTC and showing IST, when the week starts.> \n5. How are classes entered (one-time or weekly)?> \n6. Gap rule: 15 minutes by default and 25 after a 60 minute block or the third block in a row (unconfirmed).> \n7. Extra burnout rules: meal windows, end-of-day cutoff, rest day.> \n8. The exact scoring formula.> \n9. All group rules in section 11. check this and lets discuss about this ",
    "Reading through the design doc carefully before we discuss.\n\nThe doc is well-structured for a learning project. Let me go through section 11 (group feature) systematically, flagging what's decided, what's genuinely open, and where I'd push back or suggest a direction.\n\n---\n\n## Group Feature Discussion\n\n### What's already solid\n\n- Common free slots are computed, not stored — consistent with the core principle.\n- A slot is only available if booking it won't break a member's limits. Good. This belongs on the backend.\n- Concurrency via database transactions is the right call.\n\n---\n\n### Open questions, one by one\n\n**1. How are groups created and joined?**\n\nInvite code is simpler to implement and teach (generate a random code, store it, validate on join). Approval flows require async state (pending/accepted/rejected) and more API work. For v1 with 10 users who likely know each other, invite code is enough. Keep approval for v2.\n\n**2. Can a user be in several groups?**\n\nPractically yes — students are in multiple study groups. The data model already supports this (Group has members, so it's a many-to-many). There's no scheduling conflict risk since a group booking still checks each member's individual limits. I'd allow multiple groups in v1.\n\n**3. What do members see of each other?**\n\nFree/busy only is the right call for v1. Task details are sensitive (what you're studying, how behind you are). It's also less to build. Start with free/busy and never need to walk it back.\n\n**4. Does a group session count toward each member's 8 and 40 block limits?**\n\nYes, it must. A group session is a real block of focused time. If it doesn't count, users can exceed the burnout limits by packing in group sessions. The backend should treat a group booking exactly like a personal block when checking limits.\n\n**5. Does everyone need to accept, or does first booking win?**\n\nThis is the most architecturally significant question. Two options:\n\n- **First booking wins**: simpler. One member books, it's locked. Others see it as occupied. Risk: someone books a slot others weren't ready for.\n- **All must confirm**: safer socially, but requires a pending state, notifications, and timeout logic. That's a lot of async complexity for v1.\n\nRecommendation: **first booking wins**, but the person who books sees a confirmation screen that says \"this will be booked for the group.\" Keep it simple. Add confirmations in v2 if users ask.\n\n**6. Who can cancel or change a booking?**\n\nTwo reasonable choices: the person who booked it, or any member. \"Any member can cancel\" is more flexible but could cause chaos. \"Only the booker can cancel\" is simpler and more predictable. I'd go with: **only the booker can cancel, any member can propose a change (which the booker then confirms)**. But for v1, simplify further: only the booker can cancel, no change flow — just cancel and rebook.\n\n**7. Double booking prevention**\n\nThe doc already says database transactions. That's correct. The implementation pattern is: wrap the slot availability check and the insert into a single serializable transaction (or use `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the relevant rows). This is a good concurrency lesson. Worth calling out explicitly in the learning plan.\n\n---\n\n### Things the doc doesn't address yet that matter\n\n**Who can see the group's free slots?**\nOnly members, presumably. The API needs to enforce this — a non-member calling `GET /groups/{id}/free-slots` should get a 403.\n\n**What is a \"group free slot\" exactly?**\nIt's the intersection of all members' free time, filtered to slots where every member has room under their limits. This is a non-trivial computation: you need to intersect N users' busy intervals. It should follow the same interval logic as the personal scheduler. Worth noting in section 8 that the group free-slot algorithm is a generalisation of the personal one.\n\n**Does a group booking create a Block record for each member?**\nIt should. Otherwise the limit checks won't work — the backend needs a block row per member to count toward their 8/40. The `group_booking` table links them, but individual `block` rows are what the limit checker reads.\n\n**What's the minimum group size?**\nPresumably 2. Worth stating.\n\n**Can a group have a maximum size?**\nNot critical for v1 with 10 users total, but if you have 3 groups of 4 people who all overlap, the intersection might always be empty. Something to mention as a known usability risk, not a blocker.\n\n---\n\n### Suggested decisions for v1\n\n| Question | Recommendation |\n|---|---|\n| Join method | Invite code only |\n| Multiple groups per user | Allowed |\n| Visibility | Free/busy only |\n| Counts toward limits | Yes, always |\n| Booking model | First booking wins |\n| Cancel rights | Booker only; cancel and rebook instead of edit |\n| Concurrency | `SELECT FOR UPDATE` inside a transaction |\n| Block rows | One per member on booking |\n| Min group size | 2 |\n\n---\n\n### One design tension to flag\n\nSection 6 says \"suggestions are never stored as facts.\" Group free slots follow the same rule — they're computed on demand. But a group *booking* is a fact and must be stored. Make sure the data model clearly distinguishes `group_free_slot` (computed, never stored) from `group_booking` (stored, creates block rows). The current entity table has `group_booking` which is right, just make sure there's no temptation to cache the free-slot computation.\n\n---\n\nWhat would you like to dig into further — the concurrency mechanics, the free-slot intersection algorithm, or the booking/block relationship?\n[Tool uses: none]",

Stick with it.**\n\nHere's why it fits this specific project better than the alternatives:\n\n- The scheduler is pure logic with no side effects. Go's simplicity (no classes, no magic, explicit everything) is actually an advantage here — you'll write the interval logic in plain functions and it'll be easy to test in isolation, exactly what section 8 asks for.\n- The concurrency chapter (double-booking prevention) maps directly to things Go was designed for. That sounds annoying, but for a project where every rejected action needs a clear reason (your own requirement), it builds the right habits.\n- The REST API layer in Go is straightforward with the standard library alone. You don't need a framework to start.\n- What you learn in Go transfers directly to systems thinking, which is more durable than framework-specific knowledge.\n\n**The tradeoff:** The first two weeks will be slow.
