    "This changes the answer. Job market matters, and you're right to flag it.\n\nLet me be straight with you.\n\n---\n\n## The honest job market picture (India, 2026)\n\n**MERN (MongoDB, Express, React, Node.js)** is the most commonly listed stack in entry-level and internship job postings in India. Recruiters recognise it by name. Your resume saying \"MERN stack\" gets parsed faster by non-technical HR screens.\n\n**Go + Flutter** is a strong stack but it's a specialist stack. Companies that use Go are usually product companies, startups at scale, or infra teams. They exist, they pay well, but there are fewer entry-level openings compared to MERN/full-stack web roles.\n\n**Flutter specifically** is a mobile-only skill. If your goal is to become a general developer and get hired, Flutter narrows your options. Web developers are hired far more broadly than mobile developers at the entry level in India.\n\n---\n\n## The real question\n\nWhat kind of developer do you want to be?\n\n- **Web developer (frontend + backend):** MERN is the right stack. React is everywhere. Node/Express is learnable fast. MongoDB works for simple projects though it has real tradeoffs.\n- **Mobile developer:** Flutter + Dart, but know this is a narrower market.\n- **Backend/systems developer:** Go or Java Spring Boot. Fewer jobs but higher quality ones.\n\n---\n\n## My recommendation for a student looking for jobs\n\n**Switch the stack to MERN, but keep PostgreSQL instead of MongoDB.**\n\nHere is why:\n\nReact + Node.js + Express are on almost every job description. Learning them on this project means every feature you build is also portfolio evidence of industry-relevant skills.\n\nMongoDB is the default in MERN but it is genuinely the wrong database for this project. Your scheduler has hard relational constraints, transactions, and interval logic. MongoDB will fight you at every step. PostgreSQL with Node.js (using a library like `pg` or Prisma) is better technically and also teaches you SQL, which every job expects regardless of stack.\n\nSo: **React Native or React (web) + Node.js + Express + PostgreSQL.**\n\nOne more decision: **React Native vs Flutter.**\n- If you want mobile only: Flutter is fine but narrow. React Native uses JavaScript which you'll already know from React, so the skill transfers.\n- If you are open to building this as a web app instead: drop mobile entirely, use React for the frontend. Web apps are easier to deploy, easier to demo, and more relevant to most job descriptions.\n\n---\n\n## My actual suggestion\n\nBuild this as a **web app**, not a mobile app.\n\nStack: **React + Node.js + Express + PostgreSQL**\n\nReasons:\n- Every skill transfers directly to job requirements\n- Easier to deploy and share (just a URL, no APK)\n- React is the most demanded frontend skill in India by a large margin\n- Node.js means one language (JavaScript) across frontend and backend, which reduces cognitive load while learning\n- PostgreSQL teaches you real SQL and relational thinking, which is valued everywhere\n- The scheduler logic, REST API, auth, concurrency — everything in your learning plan still applies exactly\n\nThe only thing you lose is Flutter. And Flutter, for a job-seeking student targeting the broad developer market, is the weakest part of your original stack.\n\n---\n\n## Decision table\n\n| Layer | Original | Recommended | Why |\n|---|---|---|---|\n| Frontend | Flutter | React (web) | Most hired skill, transfers everywhere |\n| Backend | Go | Node.js + Express | Same language as frontend, huge job market |\n| Database | PostgreSQL | PostgreSQL | Keep this, it's the right call |\n| Auth | JWT | JWT | Same |\n| State mgmt | Provider | React Context or Zustand | Simple, learnable |\n\n---\n\nYour call. But if I were advising a student who wants to get hired: **React + Node + PostgreSQL, built as a web app.** Everything in your design doc still holds — the scheduler, the rules, the groups, the burnout limits — none of that changes. Only the frontend technology changes.\n\nWhat do you want to do?\n[Tool uses: none]",

Finish one completely, deploy it, then start the second.\n\n---\n\n## The plan\n\n**Branch 1 — Web first (MERN-ish)**\nStack: React + Node.js + Express + PostgreSQL\nWhy first: JavaScript across the stack reduces friction while you're learning the domain. You know exactly what the API needs to do, what the database schema looks like, what edge cases exist. You can focus entirely on learning Go and Flutter without also figuring out the product.\n\n---\n\n## Git structure\n\n```\nmain\n├── branch: mern         ← build this first, fully\n└── branch: go-flutter   ← start this after mern is deployed\n```\n\nKeep `main` as the design doc and decisions only — no code. Some I can recommend directly, some need your input.\n\n---\n\n**Q1. Confirm Go and PostgreSQL.**\nAnswered in techstack.md. Go + PostgreSQL for Branch 2, Node + PostgreSQL for Branch 1. Closed.\n\n---\n\n**Q2. How do weights and ranks combine?**\n\nHere's a concrete formula proposal:\n\n```\npriority_score = (goal_weight × 0.5) + (goal_rank_score × 0.3) + (deadline_urgency × 0.2)\n```\n\n- `goal_weight` — a number the user sets, e.g. 1 to 5. Normalise to 0–1 by dividing by 5.\n- `goal_rank_score` — if user ranks goals 1st, 2nd, 3rd, convert to a score: `(total_goals - rank + 1) / total_goals`. So rank 1 of 3 goals = 3/3 = 1.0, rank 3 = 1/3 = 0.33.\n- `deadline_urgency` — `1 / days_until_deadline`, capped at 1. A task due today = 1.0, due in 10 days = 0.1.\n\nHigher score = suggested first. Ties broken by deadline (earlier deadline wins), then by task creation time (older task wins).\n\nDo you want to go with this or adjust the weights (0.5 / 0.3 / 0.2)?\n\n---\n\n**Q3. Which repeat patterns are in v1, and how are they stored?**\n\nProposed v1 patterns — keep it small:\n- None (one-time)\n- Daily\n- Weekly (same day each week)\n- Weekdays only (Mon–Fri)\n\nStorage: store as a string enum on the task row — `none`, `daily`, `weekly`, `weekdays`. Store the original task as the \"template.\" Each scheduled occurrence is a separate Block row. Do not generate infinite rows — generate only for the current week on demand.\n\nDoes this cover your real use cases, or do you need anything else like \"every 2 weeks\"?\n\n---\n\n**Q4. Time rules — smallest unit, UTC vs IST, week start.**\n\nProposals:\n- Smallest time unit: **5 minutes.** Slots snap to 5-minute boundaries (e.g. 9:00, 9:05). Simple and clean.\n- Storage: **store all times as UTC in the database.** Display in IST in the app. One conversion point, no ambiguity. IST is UTC+5:30, no DST, so the conversion is always the same fixed offset.\n- Week start: **Monday.** Standard for academic schedules. The 40-block weekly limit resets every Monday 00:00 IST.\n\nAgree with these?\n\n---\n\n**Q5. How are classes entered?**\n\nProposal: one entry form, two options the user picks — \"one-time\" or \"weekly (repeats every week on this day and time).\" That covers 95% of college schedules. No other repeat options for fixed events in v1.\n\n---\n\n**Q6. Gap rule.**\n\nProposal to confirm: **15 minutes after any block under 60 minutes, 25 minutes after a 60-minute block or after the third consecutive block.** This is what the doc already floated. Agree?\n\n---\n\n**Q7. Extra burnout rules — meal windows, end-of-day cutoff, rest day.**\n\nThese need your input:\n\n- **Meal windows:** Should the app block scheduling during lunch and dinner? Proposed: block 13:00–14:00 (lunch) and 20:00–21:00 (dinner) by default, user can change in settings.\n- **End-of-day cutoff:** No blocks after what time? Proposed: 22:00 IST by default, user can change.\n- **Rest day:** Should Sunday be a no-schedule day by default? Or leave it open and let the user decide?\n\nWhat feels right to you?\n\n---\n\n**Q8. Exact scoring formula.**\nCovered in Q2 above.\n\n---\n\nOnce you answer Q2, Q3, Q6, and Q7 above, all 18 open questions are closed and we can move straight to the schema and Git setup.\n[Tool uses: none]",

          "description": "Code intelligence to analyze code with AST parsing and fuzzy search. Language auto-detected from file extension.\n\nIMPORTANT: Prefer this tool over fs_read for code files. This tool intelligently provides structured code analysis.\n\nCORE FEATURES:\n• Fuzzy search for symbols (classes, functions, methods)\n• Extracts function/class signatures via AST\n• Structural AST search and rewrite (ast-grep)\n• Codebase overview and directory exploration\n\nNOTE: Use fs_read with line ranges for unsupported patterns.\n\n## Operations\n\n**search_symbols** - Find symbol definitions by name across workspace.\nParams: symbol_name (required), path, symbol_type, limit, language, exact_match\nUses fuzzy matching by default. Set exact_match=true for precise matching.\n\n**lookup_symbols** - Batch lookup specific symbols (max 10).\nParams: symbols (required), file_path, include_source\nSet include_source=false for large classes/structs to avoid context overflow.\nScoped lookup: Provide file_path to search within specific file only.\n\n**get_document_symbols** - List all symbols in a file.\nParams: file_path (required), top_level_only (recommended: true)\nUse this for understanding file structure without reading content.\nPrefer this over fs_read when you need symbol information.\n\n**pattern_search** - AST-based structural search using ast-grep.\nParams: pattern, language (required), file_path, limit\n\n**pattern_rewrite** - AST-based code transformation.\nParams: pattern, replacement, language (required), file_path, limit, dry_run\nUse dry_run=true first to preview changes.\n\n## Pattern Search & Rewrite\n\nMetavariables:\n• $VAR - Matches single node (identifier, expression)\n• $$$ - Matches zero or more nodes (statements, parameters)\n\nSimple patterns:\n• console.log($ARG) - Match any console.log call\n• function $NAME($$$PARAMS) {} - Match function declaration\n• $OBJ.$METHOD() - Match any method call\n\nStructural rules (YAML):\n• pattern - Match code structure\n• kind - Match AST node type (function_declaration, class_declaration)\n• has - Node contains descendant matching pattern\n• inside - Node is inside ancestor matching pattern\n• all/any/not - Logical operators\n\nCritical: For relational rules (has, inside), always use stopBy: end\n\nRewrite examples:\n• pattern='var $N = $V', replacement='const $N = $V'\n• pattern='$O.hasOwnProperty($P)', replacement='Object.hasOwn($O, $P)'\n\nWorkflow:\n1. Use pattern_search first to verify matches\n2. Review matches to ensure correctness\n3. Test rewrite on small subset\n4. Apply to full codebase after verification\n\n**generate_codebase_overview** - ONLY for explicit architecture questions.       {
        "ToolSpecification": {
          "name": "web_search",
          "description": "WebSearch looks up information that is outside the model's training data or cannot be reliably inferred from the current codebase/context.\nTool performs basic compliance wrt content licensing and restriction.\nAs an agent you are responsible for adhering to compliance and attribution requirements.\nIMPORTANT: The snippets often contain enough information to answer questions - only use web_fetch if you need more detailed content from a specific webpage.\n\n## When to Use\n- When the user asks for current or up-to-date information (e.g., pricing, versions, technical specs) or explicitly requests a web search.\n- When verifying information that may have changed recently, or when the user provides a specific URL to inspect.\n\n## When NOT to Use\n- When the question involves basic concepts, historical facts, or well-established programming syntax/technical documentation.\n- When the topic does not require current or evolving information.\n\nFor any code-related tasks, follow this order:\n1. Search within the repository (if tools are available) and check if it can be inferred from existing code or documentation.\n2. Use this tool only if still unresolved and the library/data is likely new/unseen.\n\n## Content Compliance Requirements\nYou MUST adhere to strict licensing restrictions and attribution requirements when using search results:\n\n### Attribution Requirements\n- ALWAYS provide inline links to original sources using format: [description](url)\n- If not possible to provide inline link, add sources at the end of file\n- Ensure attribution is visible and accessible\n\n### Verbatim Reproduction Limits\n- NEVER reproduce more than 30 consecutive words from any single source\n- Track word count per source to ensure compliance\n- Always paraphrase and summarize rather than quote directly\n- Add compliance note when the content from the source is rephrased: \"Content was rephrased for compliance with licensing restrictions\"\n\n### Content Modification Guidelines\n- You MAY paraphrase, summarize, and reformat content\n- You MUST NOT materially change the underlying substance or meaning\n- Preserve factual accuracy while condensing information\n- Avoid altering core arguments, data, or conclusions\n\n## Usage Details\n- You may rephrase user queries to improve search effectiveness\n- You can make multiple queries to gather comprehensive information\n- Consider breaking complex questions into focused searches\n- Refine queries based on initial results if needed\n\n## Output Usage\n- Prioritize latest published sources based on publishedDate\n- Prefer official documentation to blogs and news posts\n- Use domain information to assess source authority and reliability\n\n## Error Handling\n- If unable to comply with content restrictions, explain limitations to user\n- Suggest alternative approaches when content cannot be reproduced\n- Prioritize compliance over completeness when conflicts arise\n\n## Output\nThe tool returns a JSON object with a \"results\" array containing search results:\n\n{\n  \"results\": [\n    {\n      \"title\": \"Example Page Title\",\n      \"url\": \"https://example.com/page\",\n      \"snippet\": \"Brief excerpt from the page...\",\n      \"publishedDate\": \"2025-11-20T10:30:00Z\",\n      \"domain\": \"example.com\",\n      \"id\": \"unique-id-123\",\n      \"maxVerbatimWordLimit\": 30,\n      \"publicDomain\": false\n    }\n  ]\n}\n\n## UI FROM LLM (You) back to the user\nCRITICAL: Always start your response with \"Here's what I found:\" and then start from a newline.\nALWAYS end your response with a blank line followed by 'References:' and list the sources you used in sequential order [1], [2], [3], etc. with NO gaps in numbering. Format: '[N] Title - URL' one per line. Truncate long titles to 80 characters and long URLs to 100 characters, adding '...' if truncated.",
          "input_schema": {
            "json": {
              "required": [
                "query"
              ],
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "query": {
                  "description": "Search query - can be keywords, questions, or specific topics",
                  "type": "string"
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      },
      {
        "ToolSpecification": {
          "name": "fs_write",
          "description": "A tool for creating and editing files\n * The `create` command will override the file at `path` if it already exists as a file, and otherwise create a new file\n * The `append` command will add content to the end of an existing file, automatically adding a newline if the file doesn't end with one. The file must exist.\n Notes for using the `str_replace` command:\n * The `old_str` parameter should match EXACTLY one or more consecutive lines from the original file. Be mindful of whitespaces!\n * If the `old_str` parameter is not unique in the file, the replacement will not be performed. Make sure to include enough context in `old_str` to make it unique\n * The `new_str` parameter should contain the edited lines that should replace the `old_str`.",
          "input_schema": {
            "json": {
              "properties": {
                "path": {
                  "description": "Absolute path to file or directory, e.g. `/repo/file.py` or `/repo`.",
                  "type": "string"
                },
                "summary": {
                  "description": "A brief explanation of what the file change does or why it's being made.",
                  "type": "string"
                },
                "command": {
                  "type": "string",
                  "enum": [
                    "create",
                    "str_replace",
                    "insert",
                    "append"
                  ],
                  "description": "The commands to run. Allowed options are: `create`, `str_replace`, `insert`, `append`."
                },
                "insert_line": {
                  "type": "integer",
                  "description": "Required parameter of `insert` command. The `new_str` will be inserted AFTER the line `insert_line` of `path`."
                },
                "file_text": {
                  "type": "string",
                  "description": "Required parameter of `create` command, with the content of the file to be created."
                },
                "new_str": {
                  "description": "Required parameter of `str_replace` command containing the new string. Required parameter of `insert` command containing the string to insert. Required parameter of `append` command containing the content to append to the file.",
                  "type": "string"
                },
                "old_str": {
                  "description": "Required parameter of `str_replace` command containing the string in `path` to replace.",
                  "type": "string"
                }
              },
              "required": [
                "command",
                "path"
              ],
              "type": "object"
            }
          }
        }
      },

        "ToolSpecification": {
          "name": "introspect",
          "description": "Use ONLY when the user is asking about this chat application's own features, slash commands, settings, or capabilities. Do NOT use for general coding questions, AWS help, or tasks the user wants you to perform. When mentioning commands in your response, always prefix them with '/' (e.g., '/save', '/load', '/context'). CRITICAL: Only provide information explicitly documented. If details about any tool, feature, or command are not documented, clearly state the information is not available rather than generating assumptions.",
          "input_schema": {

      {
        "ToolSpecification": {
          "name": "grep",
          "description": "Fast text pattern search in files using regex. ALWAYS use this tool instead of 'grep', 'rg', or 'ag' commands in bash. Respects .gitignore.\n\n## Text Discovery Only\nUse grep for literal text/pattern matching: error messages, TODOs, config values, regex patterns.\n\n## For Semantic Code Understanding → Use 'code' tool if available\n- Finding symbol definitions or usages → code tool (search_symbols, goto_definition, find_references)\n- Understanding code structure/relationships → code tool\n- Distinguishing definition vs call vs import → code tool\n\n## Fallback\nIf the 'code' tool is available but returns insufficient symbol info, use grep to discover candidate files/lines, then return to 'code' for precise navigation.\n\nWhen you use this tool, prefer to show the user a small list of representative matches (including file paths and line numbers) instead of only giving a high-level summary.",
          "input_schema": {
            "json": {
              "required": [
                "pattern"
              ],
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "max_files": {
                  "description": "Max number of files returned (output limit). Increase for comprehensive codebase searches.",
                  "type": "integer"
                },
                "max_total_lines": {
                  "description": "Max total matched lines returned across all files (output limit). Increase when searching for many occurrences.",
                  "type": "integer"
                },
                "max_matches_per_file": {
                  "type": "integer",
                  "description": "Max matches returned per file (output limit). Increase to see all occurrences in a file."
                },
                "pattern": {
                  "type": "string",
                  "description": "Regex pattern to search for. Examples: \"fn main\", \"class.*Component\", \"TODO|FIXME\". Start with simple patterns first (e.g. just the word you're looking for), then refine if needed."
                },
                "max_depth": {
                  "type": "integer",
                  "description": "Max directory depth to traverse when searching (search limit). Increase for deeply nested structures."
                },
                "path": {
                  "description": "Directory to search from. Defaults to current working directory.",
                  "type": "string"
                },
                "case_sensitive": {
                  "type": "boolean",
                  "description": "Case-sensitive search. Defaults to false (case-insensitive)."
                },
                "output_mode": {
                  "description": "Output format: 'content' returns matches as 'file:line:content' (default, best for seeing actual matches), 'files_with_matches' returns only file paths, 'count' returns match counts per file.",
                  "type": "string",
                  "enum": [
                    "content",
                    "files_with_matches",
                    "count"
                  ]
                },
                "include": {
                  "type": "string",
                  "description": "File filter glob. Examples: \"*.rs\", \"*.{ts,tsx}\", \"*.py\""
                }
              }
            }
          }
        }
      },
      {
        "ToolSpecification": {
          "name": "session",
          "description": "Adjust session settings temporarily (in-memory only, cleared on exit). CRITICAL: You MUST use introspect tool FIRST to verify setting names and understand their purpose before using set operation.\n\n## Session vs Persistent Settings\n- **session tool**: Temporary in-memory changes (cleared when chat exits) - Use for quick experiments or one-time adjustments\n- **fs_write tool**: Permanent changes saved to disk - Use when user says \"save\", \"persist\", \"permanently\", or \"always\"\n  - Global settings: ~/.kiro/settings.json\n  - Workspace settings: .kiro/settings.json\n\n## When to Use Each Tool\n- User: \"disable markdown\" → session tool (temporary)\n- User: \"disable markdown permanently\" → fs_write to ~/.kiro/settings.json (global) or .kiro/settings.json (workspace)\n- User: \"save this setting\" → fs_write (persistent)\n- User: \"try disabling markdown\" → session tool (temporary)\n\n## REQUIRED Workflow for Setting Changes\n1. User asks to change a setting\n2. Use introspect tool to find the correct setting name and understand what it does\n3. Determine if temporary (session) or permanent (fs_write)\n4. Use appropriate tool\n\n## Operations\n- **list**: Show currently configured session settings (non-default values only)\n- **get**: Get the current value of a specific setting\n- **set**: Change a setting value temporarily (MUST verify setting name with introspect first)\n- **reset**: Clear session override for a specific setting, or all session overrides if no key provided\n\n## Example Workflows\nTemporary change:\n  User: \"disable markdown\"\n  1. introspect(query=\"markdown setting\") → learn about chat.disableMarkdownRendering\n  2. session(operation=\"set\", key=\"chat.disableMarkdownRendering\", value=true)\n\nReset single setting:\n  User: \"reset markdown setting\"\n  session(operation=\"reset\", key=\"chat.disableMarkdownRendering\")\n\nReset all session overrides:\n  User: \"clear all my temporary settings\"\n  session(operation=\"reset\")\n\nPermanent change:\n  User: \"disable markdown permanently\"\n  1. introspect(query=\"markdown setting\") → learn about chat.disableMarkdownRendering\n  2. fs_write to modify ~/.kiro/settings.json with {\"chat.disableMarkdownRendering\": true}\n\nDO NOT guess setting names - always verify with introspect first.",
          "input_schema": {
            "json": {
              "type": "object",
              "properties": {
                "key": {
                  "type": "string",
                  "description": "Setting key (e.g., 'chat.disableMarkdownRendering'). Required for 'get' and 'set' operations. Optional for 'reset' (if omitted, resets all session overrides). MUST be verified with introspect tool first."
                },
                "value": {
                  "description": "Value to set. Type depends on the setting (boolean, string, or number). Required for 'set' operation"
                },
                "operation": {
                  "enum": [
                    "list",
                    "get",
                    "set",
                    "reset"
                  ],
                  "description": "The operation to perform: 'list' shows configured settings, 'get' retrieves a specific setting, 'set' changes a setting value temporarily, 'reset' clears session override(s)",
                  "type": "string"
                }
              },
              "required": [
                "operation"
              ]
            }
          }
        }
      }
    ]
